title: Reply to Statutory Demand Notice under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
whenToUse: Use when responding to a 15-day Section 138 statutory demand notice, rebutting the presumption of enforceable debt and asserting security cheque misuse or failure of consideration.
variantComparisonNote: Formal advocate reply notice to pre-empt criminal proceedings. Distinct from formal court written statement in trial.
youWillNeed: Copy of received demand notice, proof of commercial contract, bank ledger showing prior payments, communications demonstrating security nature of cheque.
legalBasis: Section 138 Proviso (b), Section 139 Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881; Krishna Janardhan Bhat v. Dattatraya G. Hegde (2008); Basalingappa v. Mudibasappa (2019).
mandatoryStatutoryIngredients: Specific denial of existing legally enforceable debt on date of cheque
Assertion of security instrument status or discharge through alternative mode
Call upon payee to return instrument within 7 days

particulars.label: Payee / Claimant Name
particulars.description: Name of payee who sent notice

particulars.label: Cheque Number
particulars.description: Cheque number referred in demand notice

aiBlocks.title: Preliminary Objections on Maintainability
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Draft aggressive preliminary objections showing absence of legally enforceable debt, misuse of undated security leaf, and non-maintainability of notice.

aiBlocks.title: Para-wise Defense & Security Cheque Misuse
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Provide para-wise denial of allegations in demand notice, detailing contractual breakdown, failure of consideration, and breach of trust by payee.

aiBlocks.title: Closing Demands & Warning of Legal Action
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Issue peremptory demand to return dishonoured instrument within 7 days, warning of criminal action under Section 316/318 BNS, 2023 if false complaint is filed.
